This Petition, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Made The Following:
 Order

1. This petition is filed challenging the registration of an FIR for offences punishable under Sections 3, 4 and 5 of Prize Chits and Money Circulation Schemes (Banning) Act, 1978 (for short 'the Act')
and also for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 120B read with Section 34 of IPC.

entities.text: Prize Chits and Money Circulation Schemes (Banning) Act, 1978
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. Learned SPP, at the outset, concedes that the FIR registered for offences under Sections 3, 4 and 5 of Prize Chits and Money Circulation Schemes (Banning) Act, 1978, would be incorrect and he submits that investigation for the offences would be confined only to the offences under Sections 420, 120B and Section 34 of IPC.

entities.text: Prize Chits and Money Circulation Schemes (Banning) Act, 1978
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In the light of the above, FIR and Charge sheet insofar as it incorporates the offences under Sections 3, 4 and 5 of the Act alleged against the petitioners shall stand quashed.
4. It is to be noticed that this Court in Crl.P.No.6170/2016 had reserved liberty to the authorities to proceed from the stage receiving complaint in accordance with law.

5. In WP.Nos.36587-36591/2018 and WP.Nos.37168- 37187/2018, this Court had in fact stated as follows in para '8':
"Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the submissions of learned HCGP, it is directed that in respect of offences punishable under Sections 406 & 420 of IPC, if any, the police shall hold inquiry and proceed further, after following the guidelines contained in Lalita Kumari's case and the Guidelines dated Mr S Karthik Sharma vs The State Of Karnataka on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162913510/
2 26.10.2016 (Annexure-D) issued by the Union of India."
NC: 2024:KHC:21154 6.

entities.text: S Karthik Sharma vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the above, it is clear that the police are at liberty to proceed with the investigation of the complaint but the investigation shall be only for the offences punishable under Section 406 and 420 of IPC.
The petitions are accordingly disposed of.
